message.content:
Here’s a classic, hearty lasagna recipe that serves about 8 people. It’s a layered dish of pasta sheets, rich meat sauce, creamy béchamel, and plenty of cheese—perfect for a family dinner or a potluck.

---

## Classic Beef Lasagna (Serves 8)

### Ingredients

| Ingredient | Quantity | Notes |
|------------|----------|-------|
| **Lasagna noodles** | 12–15 sheets (no-boil or regular) | If using regular, boil until al dente, then drain and set aside. |
| **Ground beef** | 1 lb (450 g) | 80/20 lean-to-fat ratio works best for flavor. |
| **Italian sausage** | ½ lb (225 g) | Optional; adds extra depth. |
| **Onion** | 1 medium | Finely chopped. |
| **Garlic cloves** | 3 | Minced. |
| **Canned crushed tomatoes** | 28 oz (800 g) | Whole peeled tomatoes crushed in a blender or use pre‑crushed. |
| **Tomato paste** | 2 tbsp | Adds richness. |
| **Water or beef broth** | 1 cup (240 ml) | For the sauce. |
| **Red wine** | ¼ cup (60 ml) | Optional but recommended. |
| **Olive oil** | 2 tbsp | For sautéing. |
| **Salt & pepper** | To taste | |
| **Dried oregano** | 1 tsp | |
| **Dried basil** | 1 tsp | |
| **Fresh parsley** | 2 tbsp | Chopped, for garnish. |
| **Ricotta cheese** | 15 oz (425 g) | |
| **Mozzarella cheese** | 16 oz (450 g) | Shredded or sliced. |
| **Parmesan cheese** | ½ cup (50 g) | Grated. |
| **Egg** | 1 | Beaten, mixed into ricotta. |
| **Béchamel sauce** | 2 cups (480 ml) | See below. |

### Béchamel Sauce (White Sauce)

| Ingredient | Quantity |
|------------|----------|
| Butter | 4 tbsp (57 g) |
| All-purpose flour | ⅓ cup (40 g) |
| Milk | 2 cups (480 ml) |
| Nutmeg | Pinch |
| Salt & pepper | To taste |

### Instructions

#### 1. Prepare the Meat Sauce
1. Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add onion and cook until translucent (~5 min).  
2. Add garlic and cook for another minute.  
3. Increase heat to medium‑high, add ground beef (and sausage if using). Break up the meat with a spoon and brown thoroughly. Drain excess fat if needed.  
4. Stir in tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, water/broth, red wine, oregano, basil, salt, and pepper. Bring to a simmer, reduce heat to low, and let it cook uncovered for 25–30 min, stirring occasionally. Adjust seasoning as needed.  

#### 2. Make the Béchamel Sauce
1. In a saucepan, melt butter over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook for 1–2 min to form a roux (do not brown).  
2. Gradually whisk in milk, ensuring no lumps form. Cook, whisking constantly, until the sauce thickens and coats the back of a spoon (~5 min).  
3. Season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Remove from heat.  

#### 3. Assemble the Lasagna
1. Preheat oven to 375 °F (190 °C). Grease a 9×13 inch baking dish.  
2. Spread a thin layer of meat sauce on the bottom of the dish.  
3. Place a single layer of lasagna noodles over the sauce.  
4. Spoon half of the béchamel sauce over the noodles, then spread half of the ricotta mixture (ricotta + beaten egg + a pinch of salt).  
5. Sprinkle a third of the shredded mozzarella and a third of the grated Parmesan.  
6. Repeat layers: sauce → noodles → béchamel → ricotta → cheeses. Finish with a top layer of noodles, remaining sauce, béchamel, ricotta, mozzarella, and Parmesan.  
7. Cover loosely with foil (to prevent sticking, spray foil with cooking spray). Bake for 25 min.  
8. Remove foil, bake an additional 15–20 min until the top is golden and bubbly.  

#### 4. Rest & Serve
1. Let the lasagna rest for 10–15 min before cutting. This helps it set and makes slicing easier.  
2. Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.  

Enjoy your homemade lasagna with a side salad, garlic bread, or a simple green vegetable for a complete meal!

---

### Tips & Variations

| Variation | How to Adapt |
|-----------|--------------|
| **Vegetarian** | Replace meat with sautéed mushrooms, spinach, zucchini, and/or lentils. Use vegetable broth instead of beef broth. |
| **Chicken** | Substitute ground chicken for beef; keep the same seasonings. |
| **Pesto Layer** | Add a thin layer of basil pesto between noodle layers for a fresh twist. |
| **Cheese Swap** | Use provolone or fontina instead of mozzarella for a different melt profile. |
| **No‑Boil Noodles** | If you’re short on time, use no‑boil lasagna sheets; just add a bit more sauce to keep them moist. |

Feel free to tweak the recipe to suit your taste or dietary preferences. Happy cooking!
